region: Sagaponack · The Hamptons, Long Island, New York
about: Diosa, Spanish for “goddess,” is Wölffer Estate’s ice-wine-style dessert wine, made at the Sagaponack estate founded by Christian Wölffer in 1988 and now run by his children, Marc and Joey. Winemaker and partner Roman Roth has made Diosa for many years, and it has become one of Long Island’s most decorated sweet wines: the 2020 vintage shared Best of Show and the Governor’s Cup at the 2022 New York Wine Classic.

Long Island winters are rarely cold enough to freeze grapes on the vine, so Roth recreates the effect. Hand-picked, late-harvested grapes go straight into a commercial freezer, and the frozen fruit is pressed to release only a small amount of intensely sweet, concentrated juice. It is fermented slowly and cold, then stopped by chilling to keep natural sugar and vivid acidity. The blend changes with each vintage, usually led by Chardonnay with aromatic or high-acid grapes such as Vignoles.

Wölffer’s notes describe ripe apricot and honey aromas, then apricot jam and a rich, honeyed texture held in balance by lively acidity, so the sweetness never turns cloying. Roth considers Diosa capable of aging for decades. It is bottled in 375 ml half bottles, and the 2021 earned a Gold medal with 92 points at the 2023 New York Wine Classic.
facts: White blend, varies by vintage (typically Chardonnay-led)
Late-harvest grapes frozen after picking, then pressed (cryoextraction)
